solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Curse put on three different articles, graduate concluded

indicators.note: concluded tells us the graduate piece comes last, closing the string of articles

parts.note: an is the indefinite article used before a vowel
a is the plain indefinite article
the is the definite article
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A curse laid upon a trio of items, once a graduate had finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is only a link. The three articles are the two indefinite forms and the definite one, and 'concluded' says the graduate's degree comes at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, so the two words are synonyms.

parts.note: C is the third letter of the alphabet
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A bird spotted on the third line of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow is a familiar black bird, so it is an example of the defining word.

clue.text: Rex travelling round low part of the West Country

indicators.note: round says the mixed letters wrap about the next piece
travelling suggests the letters of the name are moving about into a new order

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A man called Rex touring a moorland stretch of south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; Exmoor is a national park on the Somerset and Devon border, which the surface's moorland ramble suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Exmoor is a moorland region in Somerset and Devon, a part of south-west England.

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys or sells on another's behalf

indicators.note: end points to the closing letter of the word very

explanation.surface: Planting an agent right at the very end of an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about spies; it means an industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant is an industrial word for a manufacturing works, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Underclothes Alec removed having restricted size and scope

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear

indicators.note: removed suggests the name's letters are shifted out of their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Alec has taken off his underwear, which seems a modest affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges ALEC as CALE. SMALLS is everyday British slang for underpants and knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something small-scale is limited in extent, the same idea as restricted size and scope.

annotationWithheld.why: Beast turned plate upside down (6): LAMINA (plate) reversed is ANIMAL, but the one reversal is signalled by the split phrase 'turned ... upside down', which the check counts as two indicators on one op, and the redo refuses dropping either word to a link

parts.note: reads like a shop's poor sales, but the consumer is one who eats and the missing interest is in food

explanation.definitionFit: Anorexia is an eating disorder marked by loss of appetite, so the eater has no interest in consuming.

indicators.note: put in says the man piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a hue is a colour or appearance
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A kind fellow turned up to make an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate, which is the adjectival sense of kind.

parts.note: with two hands a person can carry so much; what one hand holds is half of that

explanation.definitionFit: A handful is the quantity one hand can hold, which is half of what both hands carry.

clue.text: Domestic manager does not have a way to cook

indicators.note: does not have says the next words' letters are taken away

parts.note: a steward manages a household's affairs
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A household manager lacks any method of preparing food.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to cook slowly in liquid, a specific way of cooking.

definitions.meaning: stranded means left isolated and unsupported
leg before wicket is a cricket dismissal in which the batsman is out because the ball hit a leg, that is a limb

explanation.walkthrough: lbw, leg before wicket, is a way to be given out in cricket when the ball strikes the batsman's leg instead of the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on a limb means being isolated, and in cricket lbw puts the batsman out by a limb.

definitions.meaning: a breed of gundog trained to point at game
one who sets broken bones, a bonesetter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog and bone' is Cockney rhyming slang for telephone, which distracts from the two separate readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gundog breed, and a setter of bones is one who mends fractures.

clue.text: Broadcast rejected from beginning to end

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so we want what is spoken

parts.note: to reject something is to throw it out, in the past tense threw out

explanation.surface: A programme turned down by the station from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means all the way through, during the whole time from start to finish.

definitions.meaning: saying no is turning something down
a first ... is the right to buy before others, an option

explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no, and the right of first refusal is an option on a purchase.

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear

indicators.note: exchanged suggests the letters of the name are swapped around

explanation.surface: Eric swapped a fancy hat with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' turns ERIC into RICE. 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the headgear; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a whim or sudden notion, which is what a caprice is.

indicators.note: after places the deputy piece behind the shortened word
75% means three quarters of the four-letter word for cut are kept, from its front

parts.note: to clip is to cut
a mate is a deputy, as a first mate is to a captain; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A deputy follows a three-quarter cut in working conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate means the prevailing conditions, whether of weather or of opinion.

parts.note: liable means likely to suffer something, exposed to a risk

explanation.surface: A supple coin left open to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliable means flexible and easily bent, a synonym of supple.

clue.text: Husband inside greatly troubled with apathy

indicators.note: inside says the husband piece goes within the mixed letters
troubled suggests the following word's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband indoors, deeply worried and listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges GREATLY as LETARGY, and 'inside' puts H within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy and enthusiasm, which is what apathy describes.

clue.text: Teetotaller left cheese out that's crumbly

indicators.note: out here means the cheese sits outside the other pieces

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, one who does not drink

explanation.surface: A non-drinker left out some cheese that falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheese out' means Brie goes on the outside: BRI(TTL)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittle things break easily into pieces, as crumbly things do.

clue.text: One of royal entourage has no time for guide

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a courtier is a member of a monarch's court

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is too busy to act as a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier can be a tour guide employed to look after travellers, a sense common in British English.

clue.text: Small group, as lost in mountains

indicators.note: lost in says the following word's letters disappear from within the next one

parts.note: the Caucasus is a mountain range between the Black and Caspian Seas

explanation.surface: A small party goes missing in a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a small group within a party that meets to decide policy.

clue.text: The unending lust bothered private eye

indicators.note: bothered suggests the letters are agitated into a fresh order
unending says the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A detective troubled by persistent desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims LUST to LUS; 'bothered' shuffles THE and LUS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, and a private eye is a detective for hire.

indicators.note: a bridge spans a river, so the answer spans the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An attempt to put a bridge across New York's East River.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard, which is what striving means.

clue.text: Baths with serum extracted from snake

indicators.note: extracted suggests the letters are pulled out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Venom drawn off a serpent during a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushmaster is a large venomous pit viper of Central and South America.

clue.text: Week with actor, a big noise

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays

explanation.surface: A week with a showy actor causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham is an exclamation imitating a loud impact, a big noise.

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the letters climb upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts people

explanation.surface: A small attraction set on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a minor under the protection of a guardian or court.

definitions.meaning: a verb form placing action in what lies ahead
the time yet ahead of us

explanation.definitionFit: The future is a grammatical tense, and it is the time that has yet to arrive.

clue.text: Purchase from bar long time afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the long time piece after the bar

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to move things
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Buying something from a bar a long while later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying; here it means grip or mechanical advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or mechanical advantage, the same as leverage.
